questions.answer: In one period T, the progressive wave pattern travels one wavelength λ. Therefore v = λ/T. Since f = 1/T, substitution gives v = fλ.
accepted_alternatives: Uses speed = distance/time with distance λ and time T, then replaces 1/T by f.

marking_points.text: States that the wave pattern travels one wavelength in one period.
Uses speed = distance/time to write v = λ/T.
Uses f = 1/T to obtain v = fλ.

option_feedback.A: This treats the whole eight-division span as one cycle and does not correctly take the reciprocal.
option_feedback.B: This is the reciprocal of the total time for two cycles, not the frequency of individual cycles.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Two cycles take 2.0 ms, so one period is 1.0 ms and the frequency is 1000 Hz.
option_feedback.D: This takes the reciprocal of the time represented by one division rather than one complete cycle.

marking_points.text: Selects C, obtaining 1000 Hz from a period of 1.0 ms.

option_feedback.A: Multiplying v by f does not isolate wavelength and gives the wrong dimensions.
option_feedback.B: Correct. Dividing both sides of v = fλ by f gives λ = v/f.
option_feedback.C: This ratio is the reciprocal of wavelength.
option_feedback.D: Taking the reciprocal of the product is not a valid rearrangement.

marking_points.text: Selects B, correctly rearranging the wave equation to λ = v/f.

option_feedback.D: This converts kilohertz but leaves wavelength effectively in centimetres.

parts.answer: Hz × m = s⁻¹ × m = m s⁻¹, which is a speed unit.
accepted_alternatives: Frequency in s⁻¹ multiplied by wavelength in m gives m s⁻¹.

marking_points.text: Shows that Hz multiplied by metres gives m s⁻¹, or states an equivalent valid dimensional check.
